item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q003_actin_like_atpase_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, the catalytic domains are not put in one close family: Actin/HSP70 is family c.55.1.1, Hexokinase is family c.55.1.3, and Glycerol kinase is family c.55.1.4. All three families are children of superfamily c.55.1, Actin-like ATPase domain, under fold c.55, Ribonuclease H-like motif, in class c, Alpha and beta proteins (a/b). That superfamily placement is the homology-bearing statement: SCOPe treats the actin/HSP70, hexokinase, and glycerol-kinase catalytic domains as remote homologs descended from a common actin-like ATPase-domain ancestor. The inference should be limited to the shared catalytic-domain architecture and ancestral ATPase/phosphotransfer-related core; it does not justify copying the specific cellular role or substrate specificity of actin or HSP70 onto hexokinases or glycerol kinases, or vice versa, and fold/class membership alone would be weaker structural context rather than a specific family-level functional assignment.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=actin%20HSP70&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=hexokinase&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=glycerol&limit=50","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53068/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067/children?limit=100","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/53067/homology"]}]}
